title: Quotient of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring by a nonzerodivisor is Cohen–Macaulay
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension $d=\dim S$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (finite, as $S$ is Noetherian local), and assume that $S$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(S)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $S$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ be a nonzerodivisor on $S$. Then $S/xS$ is a Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension $\dim(S/xS)=d-1$, and it is Cohen–Macaulay in the same sense: $\operatorname{depth}(S/xS)\ge d-1$, i.e. the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/xS$ of $S/xS$ contains an $S/xS$-regular sequence of length $d-1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02JN (lemma-reformulate-CM, line 25319), last assertion with c = 1 ('each quotient R/(x_1,...,x_i) is a Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension dim(R) - i'), the hypothesis that x_1 is a regular sequence being equivalent there to dim R/x_1R = dim R - 1; a special case of Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052) and Lemma lemma-CM-one-g (line 25018)
